title: JOINs & Relationships
description: Reuniting tables, guarding links, and dodging JOIN traps.

questions.prompt: How many students have a matching enrollment (an INNER JOIN)?
questions.explanation: Only student 1 has a match — INNER JOIN keeps matched rows only.

questions.prompt: The intent was to join the tables. What's wrong?
questions.code:
SELECT *
FROM Students, Enrollments;  -- meant to join them
options: No JOIN condition — this is a cross join
questions.explanation: Every student paired with every enrollment — you need JOIN ... ON.

questions.prompt: Order the clauses of a JOIN query.
questions.explanation: FROM A → JOIN B → ON the condition → WHERE the filter.

questions.code:
SELECT *
FROM Students
LEFT JOIN Enrollments
___ Students.student_id = Enrollments.student_id;
questions.explanation: ON says how the tables connect; WHERE filters afterwards.

questions.prompt: Match each JOIN idea to its meaning.

pairs.definition: Only rows with a match on both sides
All left rows, NULLs where no match
Every row paired with every row

questions.explanation: Matches only, left kept, the bridge, the explosion.

questions.prompt: Which JavaScript finds students with NO enrollments?
questions.code:
SELECT name FROM Students
LEFT JOIN Enrollments
  ON Students.student_id = Enrollments.student_id
WHERE Enrollments.student_id IS NULL;
questions.explanation: LEFT JOIN + IS NULL = keep students with no matching enrollment.

questions.prompt: How many rows does this nested-loop INNER JOIN produce?
questions.explanation: id 1 matches twice, id 2 matches once — 2 + 1 = 3 rows.

questions.prompt: Why does the database reject this? (No student 999 exists.)
questions.explanation: The foreign key forbids orphans: every enrollment must point at a real student.

questions.prompt: A self-JOIN joins a table to ___.
questions.explanation: Same table, two aliases — employees paired with their managers.

questions.prompt: Which SQL does the same self-JOIN?
options: SELECT name FROM Employees WHERE manager_id = id;
questions.explanation: Two aliases of one table, joined on the manager link.
